title: Large Wheel Loader (~95–100 t class)
model_title: Large Wheel Loader (~95–100 t class, articulated, Z-bar linkage)

introduction.definition: The ~95–100 t articulated wheel loader is the mine's flexible loading unit. It reclaims ore from the ROM-pad grade-bin fingers to keep the blend on target — into trucks, or straight into the dump hopper (load-and-carry ≤ 150 m) where the pad adjoins the tipping deck — loads trucks when an excavator is down for service, and cleans up roads and pads. It steers by articulating about a centre hitch; a Z-bar linkage (tilt cylinder, bell crank and link) gives high breakout force at the bucket lip.
applications: ROM-pad reclaim and blending into the primary sizer hopper
key_points: ~95–100 t, ~650 kW class, ~11–12 m³ rock bucket (~15–17 t of bauxite per pass)
Mobile on tyres: moves quickly between pits and the ROM pad

Z-bar linkage: high breakout because rack-back uses the full-bore (head) side of the tilt cylinder through the bell crank; not parallel-lift, so the operator trims bucket angle while lifting (return-to-dig and lift kick-out set the positions)
Articulated steering: front and rear frames pivot about the centre hitch (~±40°)
Keep load-and-carry short — typically ≤ 100–150 m (ROM-pad fingers laid out within this distance of the hopper); check tyre TKPH for the shift; travel with the bucket low (~0.5 m) and racked back

introduction.summary: The ~95–100 t articulated wheel loader is the flexible loading unit of the mine: it reclaims the ROM-pad grade bins into the dump hopper for blending, back-up loads trucks when an excavator is down, cleans up spillage and moves quickly between pits on its tyres. A Z-bar linkage gives strong breakout force for digging; the machine steers by articulating about the centre hitch.

steps.text: The loader drives the bucket into the pile with the bucket flat on the floor (about 1.5 m of penetration).
The tilt cylinder extends, the bell crank turns and pulls the link, and the bucket racks back to fill it (Z-bar linkage).
The loader reverses out while articulating about the centre hitch — one steering cylinder extends while the other retracts — then drives forward to the target in a short "V".
The lift cylinders raise the arms to full lift (hinge pin ~7 m, dump clearance ~4.7 m) while travelling.
At full lift the bucket is dumped to about −45°; the ore slides out once the floor passes about −15°. The loader reverses, returns the bucket to the dig position and goes back to the pile.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Productivity = bucket payload × passes per hour; a short "V" cycle (~35–45 s) is typical for truck loading (engineering estimate).

engineering_parameters.title: Operating parameters
selection_notes: Match the loader to the truck in ~4–5 passes at rated payload. In bauxite (~1.45–1.55 t/m³ loose) an 11–12 m³ rock bucket carries ~15–17 t, so a 90 t / ~62 m³ truck takes about 5–6 passes. A ~13–14 m³ light-material bucket brings this back to ~4–5 for ore-only duty; keep a rock bucket for ferricrete caprock.

safety: Articulation pinch point: never stand between the frames — fit the frame lock for maintenance.

Reversing is the main loader hazard: camera/radar and collision avoidance (CAS), never reverse into a truck lane; on the ROM pad trucks use a one-way loop and the loader works only on its marked side.
At the dump hopper: tip only on green, approach square with the frames straight, stop with the tyres at the wheel stop, never tip while the rock breaker is working.

Tyres: inflate with nitrogen only; after any heat event (fire, lightning strike, welding/heating near the rim, brake overheating) set the OEM/site tyre exclusion zone (typically ≥ 300 m in front of the tread, ~50+ m to the side) for at least 24 h
Never work under raised arms or bucket — lower to the ground or fit the lift-arm support/lock and isolate stored hydraulic energy
Fire: hot turbo/exhaust plus hydraulic or fuel leaks; keep the fire-suppression system armed and know the manual actuator
Use three points of contact on stairs; never mount or dismount a moving machine
Stay off windrows and bench edges; keep the bucket low when travelling; sound the horn before moving (1 forward, 2 reverse)

script.narration: This module introduces the Large Wheel Loader (~95–100 t class).
The ~95–100 t articulated wheel loader is the mine's flexible loading unit.

It reclaims ore from the ROM-pad grade-bin fingers to keep the blend on target — into trucks, or straight into the dump hopper (load-and-carry ≤ 150 m) where the pad adjoins the tipping deck — loads trucks when an excavator is down for service, and cleans up roads and pads.
It steers by articulating about a centre hitch; a Z-bar linkage (tilt cylinder, bell crank and link) gives high breakout force at the bucket lip.
Typical applications include ROM-pad reclaim and blending into the primary sizer hopper; back-up truck loading; clean-up of spillage, stockpile management.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Large Wheel Loader (~95–100 t class) works.
The loader drives the bucket into the pile with the bucket flat on the floor (about 1.5 m of penetration).
The tilt cylinder extends, the bell crank turns and pulls the link, and the bucket racks back to fill it (Z-bar linkage).
The loader reverses out while articulating about the centre hitch — one steering cylinder extends while the other retracts — then drives forward to the target in a short "V".

The overlay shows the material path: pile → bucket → truck / hopper. Ore is crowded into the bucket at the pile face, racked back, lifted while the loader reverses and turns, and dumped at full lift.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Large Wheel Loader (~95–100 t class).
Walk-around: tyres (cuts, cold pressures, wheel nuts), bucket teeth, hoses, hitch, steps and rails.
Check auto-lube to hitch and linkage pins; clean the cooling cores.
Oil sampling (engine, transmission, hydraulic, axles).
Engine oil and filters; transmission and hydraulic filters.
Component change-outs by life hours (engine, transmission, axles).
Watch for tyre damage: cuts, sidewall damage. Common cause: sharp rock, wheel spin in the pile.
Watch for hitch wear: clunk when steering, play in the hitch. Common cause: lack of grease, shock loads.
Watch for bucket drift: bucket rolls forward under load. Common cause: tilt-cylinder seal leakage.
Record every inspection so trends — wear, temperatures, pressures, leaks and performance — can be compared over time.

options: By articulating the front and rear frames about the centre hitch

questions.question: What does the Z-bar linkage provide?
options: High breakout force at the bucket lip
questions.explanation: Rack-back is powered by the tilt cylinder's head side, multiplied by the bell crank near ground level.

questions.question: What is the loader's main job on the ROM pad?

options: It wears the bucket teeth faster

controls: Steering joystick or wheel, loader joystick (lift/tilt), transmission control, brake/impeller-clutch pedal, frame lock
pre_start: Walk-around; frame lock stowed; tyres and steps
Check engine, transmission, hydraulic and coolant levels; fire suppression armed; lights, horn, cameras and radar working; isolation tags removed; tyres cold-checked
start_up: Neutral and park brake on before cranking; let the automatic secondary-steering check complete
Do the service- and park-brake holding tests per OEM/site procedure before leaving the parking area; warm up
normal: Enter the pile square with the bucket flat; rack back to fill; short V-cycle to the hopper or truck
At the hopper: frames straight, approach square, front tyres against the wheel stop, dump at full lift
Keep load-and-carry ≤ 100–150 m with the bucket low (~0.5 m) and racked back
Keep the floor clean to protect tyres
shut_down: Park on level ground clear of traffic, highwalls and edges; bucket flat on the ground; transmission in neutral; park brake on; implement lockout engaged
Cool-down idle (~3–5 min); engine off; three-point dismount
alarms_interlocks: Low brake-accumulator pressure → automatic park-brake application
tips: Do not spin the tyres in the pile
Load the bucket fully but smoothly
